It's been bugging me for a while about how Dean Pees always eases up on the defensive play-calling in 2nd half when given a 2 score lead (at least 9 points) and inevitably ends up allowing the other team to just walk up and down the field for score after score. So I decided to actually look at the numbers since Pees became the defensive coordinator in 2012.

Games where the Ravens have had a 2 score lead at some point in the game: 29 out of 59 games

Blowouts for the Ravens (won by 20 points or more): 8 out of 29

Games that ended with a Ravens win despite blowing a 2 score lead: 3 out of 29 (2012 Week 9 vs. Browns, 2013 Week 5 vs. Dolphins, 2013 Week 10 vs. Bengals)

Games that ended with a Ravens win without blowing a lead, but only thanks to a missed 2 pt conversion and/or field goal: 3 out of 29 (2012 Week 6 vs. Cowboys, 2012 Super Bowl vs. 49ers, 2013 Week 13 vs. Steelers)

Games that ended with a Ravens loss after holding a 2 score lead: 6 out of 29 (2012 Week 2 vs. Philadelphia, 2012 Week 13 vs. Pittsburgh, 2013 Week 11 vs. Chicago, 2014 Week 13 vs. San Diego, 2014 Divisional Round vs. Patriots, 2015 Week 5 vs. Browns)

So there were 21 games where the Ravens led by 2 scores and the offense didn't keep putting points on the board to turn it into a blowout. (There were a couple where the Ravens didn't actually get 2 score lead until less than 5 minutes left in the 4th quarter, but I left them in since taking them out might make this is a bit more subjective than I wanted it to be.)

Of those 21 games, 12 of them the Ravens either blew the lead or barely avoided blowing the lead and only half of those 6 games ended up with a Ravens win.

When your defensive coordinator (on a defense first team) struggles to defend a lead almost 60% of the time when the team is counting on him to, I feel like it's time for a change. I sincerely hope that this is Dean Pees' last season with the Ravens, because he's not with the Patriots anymore and he can't just keep hoping that the offense is just going to keep putting up points.
